name: Supported image formats
answer:
ANSWERED BY DECISION 9, and the referee's citation correction is adopted.

Decision 9, approved: support .bmp, .gif and .webp in addition to the legacy five. So the supported set is .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .tif, .tiff, .bmp, .gif and .webp, extension case-insensitive.

THE REFEREE WAS RIGHT THAT THE CITATION CONTRADICTED ITSELF, and the reason is worth recording because it IS the defect: legacy has FOUR different lists and they disagree.

  core/file_manager.py:743                png jpg jpeg tiff tif
  utils/custom_file_system_model.py:30    the same five, as name filters
  ui/main_window.py:5386                  the five plus bmp
  ui/workers/image_discovery_worker.py:8  all eight, bmp gif webp included

So a .webp is discovered by the sequence worker and then rejected as 'not an image' by the file manager. A user who puts one in a folder sees it in one place and not another, with no message either way. Decision 9's answer is the union, which happens to be the list the sequence worker already used.

BUILT IN PHASE 2, at `modernized/lazylabel-reimagined/api/src/annotations/sidecars.ts`, as the only such list in the system, with the four legacy sources recorded beside it so nobody reintroduces a second one.

One clause of the card is preserved deliberately: only files DIRECTLY inside the chosen folder are listed, not recursively. Changing that would change which images a dataset contains, and that is a Phase 4 product decision rather than a port question - it is called out in the dataset browser's scope rather than settled here.

Separately, and this is not the same rule: which files are OFFERED as images is decided by the extension, but what they CONTAIN is checked by decoding. `AI_NATIVE_SPEC.md`'s hostile-input requirement means a .png that is not a PNG is refused by the decoder, not trusted by its name.
